messages.content: The airline changed our Monday flight home from late afternoon to early afternoon. Can you compare the changed flight with the later nonstop and the evening connection? I want total travel time, any fare difference for both of us, and how each one works with hotel checkout and returning the rental car.

Yes. I found all three options for Monday, June 22, from San Diego to Atlanta. The airline-changed nonstop leaves at 1:20 p.m. and arrives at 8:43 p.m., with 4 hours 23 minutes in the air. There is a nonstop at 5:35 p.m. arriving at 12:58 a.m., also 4 hours 23 minutes. The connecting option leaves at 6:40 p.m., changes planes in Dallas, and arrives in Atlanta at 5:54 a.m. Tuesday after 8 hours 14 minutes total. I’ll check the exact ticket and rental-car implications before recommending one.
Please do. The hotel checkout is at 11, and the car is currently due back at 11:15.

The 1:20 p.m. changed flight has no fare increase. You would need to leave Tamarack around 9:45 a.m. to allow for the drive, fuel stop, car return, and security, so it effectively eliminates the final morning and requires checkout before the stated time. The current 11:15 a.m. car return is aligned with that flight.
That is exactly what I’m trying to avoid. What would the other two cost?

Moving both tickets to the 5:35 p.m. nonstop costs $186 total, including the fare difference and change in taxes. The 6:40 p.m. connecting itinerary costs $74 total for both travelers. Neither has an additional airline change fee. Your existing outbound remains unchanged.
And the timing from Carlsbad? Could we keep the room until 11 and still have some beach time?

Yes. For the 5:35 p.m. nonstop, you could use the morning, check out at 11:00 a.m., have lunch nearby, and leave Carlsbad around 1:45 p.m. Returning the car by about 2:45 p.m. would leave a comfortable airport margin. National can extend the return from 11:15 a.m. to 2:45 p.m. for $21.60, making the combined additional cost $207.60. For the 6:40 p.m. connection, a 3:45 p.m. car return would add $32.40, and you could leave Carlsbad around 2:45 p.m. Its combined additional cost would be $106.40.
So the connection saves $101.20 compared with the later nonstop, but gets us home almost five hours later and overnight.

Correct. It also adds a plane change in Dallas and arrives Tuesday morning rather than shortly after midnight. The 5:35 p.m. nonstop costs more, but it preserves most of Monday, has the same 4-hour-23-minute travel time as the revised flight, and avoids an overnight itinerary.

The 5:35 nonstop is the sensible choice. For return flights from museum trips, when my duties finish early enough, keep prioritizing afternoon or evening departures too. I don’t need a rigid after-6 cutoff; later in the day is what matters.

Understood. For this trip, I’ll switch both passengers to the 5:35 p.m. nonstop and move the National return to 2:45 p.m. The added amount will be $207.60 total: $186 for the flights and $21.60 for the rental extension. Shall I finalize both changes using the existing payment method?
Yes, finalize them. Please confirm that Thursday’s outbound, Tamarack, and everything else remain untouched.

The changes are complete. Your Monday, June 22 return now departs San Diego at 5:35 p.m. and arrives in Atlanta at 12:58 a.m. Tuesday, nonstop, for Avery Thompson and one additional adult. The flight confirmation remains C4N8QW, and $186 was charged to the existing card. Thursday’s outbound was not changed.

National confirmation NAT-6184AV now has a return time of 2:45 p.m. on Monday, June 22; the pickup remains Thursday, June 18 at 11:30 a.m. The revised pay-later rental total is $305.76, an increase of $21.60, with no optional insurance or prepaid fuel added. Tamarack Beach Resort confirmation TBR-618224 remains unchanged for June 18-22 in the Partial Ocean View King room for two adults at $2,214.52. Its cancellation terms and included parking are unchanged. No other anniversary reservations were modified.
